checks.label: So a negative power gives the reciprocal of the number, 1 over the number: on the first screen, at every power from −1 to −6, the strip reads 4.7 times 1 over that many 10s, and its line "10ⁿ = 1 ÷ …" adds up

In standard form, numbers are recorded as a number between 1 and 10 multiplied by a power of ten: the Standard form view of the current at every power from −6 to 3, the front-number screen at 4.7 × 10⁻³, and the right answer to 470 × 10⁻⁵ each leave a front number from 1 up to 10 whose digits, slid by its power, are the number on the strip

Prefix symbols should be chosen so that numerical values are between 0.1 and 1000, and only prefixes for 10 raised to a multiple of 3 should be used: in Engineering notation, at every power from −6 to 3, the front number is from 1 up to 1000, its power is a multiple of 3 with that prefix (none at 10⁰), and front number × that power is the current on the strip
Milli (symbol m) is a unit prefix denoting a factor of one thousandth (10⁻³): in Engineering notation at power −3 the current 0.0047 A reads 4.7 mA, and the line 1 mA = 10⁻³ A = 0.001 A adds up

The base numbers are the same, so add the indices together (9³ × 9⁵ = 9⁸): 2 mA × 5 kΩ slides 3 places right for the m and 3 back for the k, landing on 10 × 10⁰ V = 10 V, and 4 mA × 2.2 kΩ lands on 8.8 V
Any base to the power of zero equals 1: the first screen at power 0 shows 10⁰ = 1 and leaves 4.7 unslid, and 10 × 10⁰ V and 8.8 × 10⁰ V sit exactly where 10 and 8.8 sit

Each step up slides every digit exactly one place left: on the first screen the number at each power is 10 times the one at the power below, and the zeros only fill places between the digits and the point
Every row drawn on every screen, in every state, reads back its own number from its digits, and every line of working adds up
The prefix changes only at every third place: in Engineering notation from 10³ down to 10⁻⁶ the prefix runs k, then none three times, m three times, µ three times
Each puzzle accepts only its right answer; the right answer's row lands on the number asked for; each wrong pick draws one row of its own in red, holding the number it names
Every demonstration has arrived within 5 s of its screen opening, nothing before the 0.35 s screen fade; every answer's motion, and every move on a live screen, within 3 s
